objective_for_doctor: A 54-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have intense coughing fits, heavy pain, and skin lesions/redness.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve been having intense coughing fits, and with that I feel heavy pain and some skin lesions/redness. The discomfort seems around both the right and left iliac fossa area, and the rash swelling feels quite bad (about 7/10).

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—first, when did the coughing fits and the skin redness/lesions start, and have you had fever or chills?  
Doctor: Also, are the skin lesions painful or itchy, and are you noticing any blisters or sores anywhere else?

The coughing fits and the skin redness/lesions started pretty fast—like within hours, maybe around 7/10 speed. I’m not sure about fever or chills; I haven’t noticed those. The rash isn’t itchy (itching 0/10), but it feels painful/heavy, and I don’t have blisters or sores anywhere else.

Doctor: Any recent new medications (especially antibiotics/NSAIDs), recent travel, or contact with anyone with a rash/respiratory infection—also, do the coughing fits produce sputum (what color) or is it dry?  
Doctor: On exam, I’d like to check your vital signs and look closely at the rash (distribution, tenderness, warmth, and whether it looks like urticaria vs a tender purplish rash); can you tell me where the skin changes are located on your body?

No recent travel. I haven’t started any new medications like antibiotics or NSAIDs, and I don’t know of any contact with someone who had a rash or respiratory infection. The coughing is with intense fits, but I’m not sure about sputum color—I think it’s mostly dry.

For the skin changes, the redness/lesions are on the area that feels connected to the pain on both sides—around the right iliac fossa and left iliac fossa. They look pale, and the lesions are larger than 1 cm, with swelling feeling severe (about 7/10).

Doctor: Thanks—so the rash is painful, non-itchy, pale, large (>1 cm), and centered over both iliac fossae with severe swelling; that pattern with rapid onset alongside intense coughing makes me want to check for an inflammatory vasculitic process or pneumonia-associated hypersensitivity, so I’d like a few urgent details: do you have any shortness of breath or chest pain, and any blood in sputum or black/bloody stools?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential + CRP/ESR  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
I don’t have shortness of breath or chest pain. I also haven’t noticed blood in my sputum, and I don’t have black or bloody stools.

Doctor: Any known history of autoimmune disease, recent viral illness, or gum/skin sores—also, is the rash fixed in the same spots (not moving) and are the lesions tender to touch or do they feel “bruised/purplish”?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis + creatinine (look for hematuria/proteinuria)  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Skin exam photo/dermatology consult if available

I don’t have any known autoimmune disease, and I haven’t had a recent viral illness that I’m aware of. I also don’t have gum sores or other skin sores besides this.

The rash is in the same spots and doesn’t seem to move, and it feels tender—more like bruised/purplish with swelling.

Doctor: Given the rapid, non-itchy painful “bruised/purplish” fixed rash with severe tenderness plus a new intense cough, I’m concerned about small/medium-vessel vasculitis or pulmonary-renal involvement; do you have any new leg swelling, joint pains, or reduced urination/color change of urine?  
Doctor: Also—on exam, are the lesions blanching (turn white when pressed) or non-blanching?

I haven’t noticed new leg swelling, and I don’t have joint pains. I also haven’t noticed reduced urination or any change in urine color.

I’m not sure about blanching—when I press the skin I don’t know if it turns white or not.

Doctor: I need 2 quick checks: have you had severe sore throat, dental infection, or recent antibiotics/NSAIDs at all in the past month—and are you currently taking any anticoagulants?  
Doctor: Lastly, when you press one of the purplish spots firmly with a clear glass/your finger for 5 seconds, does it blanch (turn pale) or stay dark?

No severe sore throat or dental infection that I know of, and I haven’t taken antibiotics or NSAIDs in the past month. I’m not currently taking any anticoagulants.

I haven’t done the glass/finger press test long enough to be sure whether it blanches or stays dark.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as urgent because a non-blanching, painful “bruised/purplish” rash with rapid onset can be vasculitis (and paired with cough we must also rule out lung involvement); can you repeat: is it definitely non-blanching, and do you have any wheeze/rapid breathing?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Skin biopsy (punch biopsy of fresh lesion) + direct immunofluorescence if available  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: BMP/CMP + blood pressure + urine microscopy (RBC casts) immediately
I can’t say definitely that it’s non-blanching—I wasn’t able to confirm that with a proper 5-second press test. I also don’t have wheeze or rapid breathing that I’ve noticed.

Doctor: Based on the rapid-onset, fixed, painful bruised/purplish-appearing larger-than-1cm lesions over both iliac fossae plus intense cough, my top concern is an inflammatory small/medium-vessel vasculitis (e.g., IgA vasculitis/HSP or ANCA-associated vasculitis) versus a severe infection/inflammatory mimic—your next step is to confirm whether the rash is truly non‑blanching and to rule out lung/renal involvement immediately.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Skin_biopsy (punch biopsy of fresh lesion) + direct immunofluorescence  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Repeat BP and full urine microscopy (RBC/protein casts) + BMP/CMP (renal function) + Urinalysis with protein/hematuria quantification  
Doctor: After we have those results (and a chest imaging read), DIAGNOSIS READY: leukocytoclastic vasculitis with possible IgA vasculitis/pulmonary involvement—pending biopsy/urinalysis and chest imaging confirmation.
